**FIFA 21 Data Analysis Project**

**Part 1: FIFA 21 Data Cleaning and Preparation**

**Project Overview**

This project cleans and prepares the FIFA 21 dataset for further analysis. The main steps include data cleaning, data quality checks, feature engineering, and the creation of summary tables.

**1.1. Setup**

```{r, echo=FALSE}
packages <- c("tidyverse", "ggplot2", "dplyr","readxl")

install.packages(
  packages,
  repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
)
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

**1.2. Load Data**

```{r,echo=TRUE}
fifa_raw <- read.csv(
  "Data Cleaning Exercise fifa21_raw_data-2.csv"
)
library(dplyr)
glimpse(fifa_raw)
```
**1.3. Data Cleaning**

**1.3.1 Remove Whitespace, Newlines, and Tabs**
```{r, echo=TRUE}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
data <- fifa_raw %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.character),
      ~ str_squish(
        str_replace_all(.x, "[\r\n\t]+", " ")
      )
    )
  )

head(data)
```
**1.3.2 Convert Height to Inches**

The original height values are converted from feet and inches into a single numerical value in inches.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
data$Height <- str_remove(data$Height, "\"")

data$Height <- as.numeric(sub(".*'", "", data$Height)) +
  12 * as.numeric(sub("'.*", "", data$Height))

head(data$Height)
```
**1.3.3 Convert Weight from Pounds to Kilograms**
```{r, echo=TRUE}
data$Weight <- as.numeric(
  str_remove(data$Weight, "lbs")
)

data$Weight <- data$Weight / 2.20462

data$Weight <- round(data$Weight, digits = 0)

head(data$Weight)
```
**1.4. Convert Financial Variables**

The variables Value, Wage, and Release Clause contain currency symbols and abbreviations such as K and M.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
money_to_number <- function(x) {
  
  x <- str_remove_all(x, "[€,$£]")
  
  multiplier <- case_when(
    str_detect(x, "M") ~ 1000000,
    str_detect(x, "K") ~ 1000,
    TRUE ~ 1
  )
  
  number <- parse_number(x)
  
  number * multiplier
}

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(Value, Wage, Release.Clause),
      money_to_number
    )
  )

head(
  data %>%
    select(Value, Wage, Release.Clause)
)
```
**1.5. Convert Star Ratings**

The variables W.F, SM, and IR contain star symbols. These are converted into numeric values.
```{r, echo=TRUE}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(W.F, SM, IR),
      ~ as.numeric(
        str_remove_all(
          as.character(.x),
          "[★☆[:space:]]"
        )
      )
    )
  )

head(
  data %>%
    select(W.F, SM, IR)
)
```

**1.6. Convert Joined Date**
```{r, echo=TRUE}
library(lubridate)
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Joined = parse_date_time(
      Joined,
      orders = c("b d, Y", "dmy", "mdy")
    ) %>%
      as.Date()
  )

head(data$Joined)
```
**1.7. Calculate Years at the Club**
```{r, echo=TRUE}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    years_at_club = round(
      time_length(
        interval(Joined, Sys.Date()),
        "years"
      ),
      2
    )
  )

head(
  data %>%
    select(Joined, years_at_club)
)
```
**1.8. Data Quality Checks**

Check Dataset Structure
```{r, echo=TRUE}
glimpse(data)
```
Check Missing Values
```{r, echo=TRUE}
colSums(is.na(data))
```
Check for Remaining Newlines and Tabs
```{r, echo=TRUE}
data %>%
  filter(
    if_any(
      where(is.character),
      ~ str_detect(.x, "[\n\r\t]")
    )
  )
```
Check for Remaining Extra Whitespace
```{r, echo=TRUE}
data %>%
  filter(
    if_any(
      where(is.character),
      ~ .x != str_squish(.x)
    )
  )
```
**1.9. Feature Engineering**

Create Key Dummy Variables
```{r, echo=TRUE}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Left = if_else(foot == "Left", 1L, 0L),
    Striker = if_else(BP == "ST", 1L, 0L),
    Goalie = if_else(BP == "GK", 1L, 0L)
  )

head(
  data %>%
    select(foot, BP, Left, Striker, Goalie)
)
```
Create Position Dummy Variables
```{r, echo=TRUE}
position_dummies <- as.data.frame(
  model.matrix(~ 0 + BP, data = data)
)

head(position_dummies)
```
Create the Field Players Dataset

Goalkeepers are removed to focus the analysis on field players.
```{r, echo=TRUE}
field_players <- data %>%
  filter(BP != "GK")

dim(field_players)
head(field_players)
```
**1.10. Dataset Overview**
```{r, echo=TRUE}
dataset_overview <- tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Number of rows",
    "Number of columns",
    "Key variables"
  ),
  
  Description = c(
    as.character(nrow(data)),
    as.character(ncol(data)),
    paste(
      c(
        "Name", "Age", "Height", "Weight",
        "Value", "Wage", "BP", "Dribbling",
        "Agility", "Interceptions"
      ),
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
)

dataset_overview
```
**1.11. Missing Values Summary**
```{r, echo=TRUE}
missing_summary <- tibble(
  Variable = names(data),
  Missing_Count = colSums(is.na(data)),
  Missing_Percentage = round(
    colSums(is.na(data)) / nrow(data) * 100,
    2
  )
) %>%
  filter(Missing_Count > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(Missing_Count))

missing_summary
```
**1.12. Residual Whitespace Check**
```{r, echo=TRUE}
whitespace_check <- tibble(
  Variable = names(data),
  
  Residual_Newlines_Tabs = sapply(data, function(x) {
    if (is.character(x)) {
      sum(
        str_detect(x, "[\r\n\t]+"),
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    } else {
      0
    }
  }),
  
  Residual_Extra_Whitespace = sapply(data, function(x) {
    if (is.character(x)) {
      sum(
        x != str_trim(str_squish(x)),
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    } else {
      0
    }
  })
)

whitespace_check
```
Summary of Whitespace Issues
```{r, echo=TRUE}
table3_summary <- whitespace_check %>%
  summarise(
    `Newline/Tab Issues` = sum(Residual_Newlines_Tabs),
    `Extra Whitespace Issues` = sum(
      Residual_Extra_Whitespace
    )
  )

table3_summary
```
**1.13. Final Dataset Summary**
```{r, echo=TRUE}
cat(
  "Original dataset dimensions:",
  dim(fifa_raw),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Cleaned dataset dimensions:",
  dim(data),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Field players dimensions:",
  dim(field_players),
  "\n"
)
```
**Conclusion**

The FIFA 21 dataset has been cleaned and prepared for further analysis.

The final datasets include:

data: The complete cleaned FIFA 21 dataset.

field_players: The dataset excluding goalkeepers.

position_dummies: Dummy variables representing player positions.

**Part 2: Predicting and Improving Player OVA**

**Project Overview**

This analysis uses a regression model to predict a center back's Overall Rating (OVA) based on key defensive and physical attributes.

The analysis focuses on O. Hüsing and uses P. Mainka as a benchmark for player development. Several improvement scenarios are created to estimate how improvements in defensive skills could affect Hüsing's predicted OVA.

**2.1 Data Preparation**

**2.1.1 Select Benchmark Players**

This analysis compares O. Hüsing with P. Mainka using key defensive and physical attributes.
```{r, echo=TRUE}
cb_benchmark <- field_players %>%
  filter(Name %in% c("P. Mainka", "O. Hüsing")) %>%
  select(
    Name,
    Age,
    X.OVA,
    POT,
    Interceptions,
    Standing.Tackle,
    Sliding.Tackle,
    Heading.Accuracy,
    Strength,
    Sprint.Speed
  )

cb_benchmark
```

**2.2 Create Player Development Targets**

Development targets are created for O. Hüsing's key defensive attributes.
```{r,echo=TRUE}
husing_target <- cb_benchmark %>%
  filter(Name == "O. Hüsing") %>%
  mutate(
    Interceptions = 76,
    Standing.Tackle = 77,
    Sliding.Tackle = 72
  )

husing_target
```
**2.3. Regression Analysis**

**2.3.1 Prepare Center Back Model Data**
```{r,echo=TRUE}
cb_model_data <- field_players %>%
  filter(BP == "CB") %>%
  select(
    X.OVA,
    Interceptions,
    Standing.Tackle,
    Sliding.Tackle,
    Heading.Accuracy,
    Strength,
    Sprint.Speed
  ) %>%
  na.omit()

head(cb_model_data)
```
**2.3.2 Build the Regression Model**

The regression model predicts OVA based on defensive and physical attributes.
```{r,echo=TRUE}
cb_model <- lm(
  X.OVA ~ Interceptions +
    Standing.Tackle +
    Sliding.Tackle +
    Heading.Accuracy +
    Strength +
    Sprint.Speed,
  data = cb_model_data
)

summary(cb_model)
```
**2.4. Model Evaluation**

**2.4.1 Check Multicollinearity**

The Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) is used to examine relationships among predictor variables.

```{r,echo=FALSE}
library(car)
```
```{r,echo=TRUE}
vif(cb_model)
```
**2.4.2 Regression Diagnostic Plots**
```{r,echo=TRUE}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

plot(cb_model)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

The diagnostic plots include:

Residuals vs Fitted

Normal Q-Q

Scale-Location

Residuals vs Leverage

**2.5. OVA Prediction and Improvement Analysis**

**2.5.1 Predict Current and Improved OVA**

First, create datasets representing Hüsing's current and improved attributes.
```{r,echo=TRUE}
husing_current <- cb_benchmark %>%
  filter(Name == "O. Hüsing") %>%
  select(
    Interceptions,
    Standing.Tackle,
    Sliding.Tackle,
    Heading.Accuracy,
    Strength,
    Sprint.Speed
  )
husing_improved <- husing_target %>%
  select(
    Interceptions,
    Standing.Tackle,
    Sliding.Tackle,
    Heading.Accuracy,
    Strength,
    Sprint.Speed
  )

husing_current
husing_improved
```
**2.5.2 Compare Current and Improved OVA**
```{r,echo=TRUE}
current_ova <- predict(
  cb_model,
  newdata = husing_current
)

improved_ova <- predict(
  cb_model,
  newdata = husing_improved
)

comparison <- data.frame(
  Scenario = c(
    "Current Hüsing",
    "Improved Hüsing"
  ),
  Predicted_OVA = c(
    current_ova,
    improved_ova
  )
)

comparison
```
**2.5.3 Calculate the Predicted OVA Change**
```{r,echo=TRUE}
predicted_change <- improved_ova - current_ova

predicted_change
```
**2.6. OVA Improvement Scenarios**

This section simulates different development scenarios to evaluate how individual improvements affect predicted OVA.

**2.6.1 Define Current Player Attributes**
```{r,echo=TRUE}
husing_current <- data.frame(
  Interceptions = 63,
  Standing.Tackle = 71,
  Sliding.Tackle = 67,
  Heading.Accuracy = 76,
  Strength = 90,
  Sprint.Speed = 55
)
husing_current
```
**2.6.2 Create Improvement Scenarios**

Scenario 1: Improve 
```{r,echo=TRUE}
scenario1 <- husing_current
scenario1$Interceptions <- 76
```
Scenario 2: Improve Standing Tackle
```{r,echo=TRUE}
scenario2 <- scenario1
scenario2$Standing.Tackle <- 77
```
Scenario 3: Improve Sliding Tackle
```{r,echo=TRUE}
scenario3 <- scenario2
scenario3$Sliding.Tackle <- 72
```
**2.6.3 Predict OVA for All Scenarios**
```{r,echo=TRUE}
result <- data.frame(
  Scenario = c(
    "Current Hüsing",
    "Improve Interceptions",
    "Improve Defensive Core",
    "Full Development Target"
  ),
  
  Predicted_OVA = c(
    predict(cb_model, husing_current),
    predict(cb_model, scenario1),
    predict(cb_model, scenario2),
    predict(cb_model, scenario3)
  )
)

result

```
**2.7. Key Results**

The regression model is used to estimate how improvements in defensive skills affect O. Hüsing's predicted OVA.

The analysis compares four scenarios:

Current Hüsing – Current player attributes.

Improve Interceptions – Interceptions increased to 76.

Improve Defensive Core – Interceptions and Standing Tackle improved.

Full Development Target – Interceptions, Standing Tackle, and Sliding Tackle improved.

The final scenario predicts the highest OVA and demonstrates how targeted player development can support improvements in overall performance.

**Conclusion**

This analysis demonstrates how regression analysis can support player development decisions.

By simulating different improvement scenarios, the model identifies how changes in key defensive attributes may affect a center back's predicted OVA. The results provide a data-driven approach for evaluating player development priorities.
